run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only Loki was reachable in this Run; the Kubernetes API, Prometheus and Jaeger all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. In Loki, namespace app-259 contains a single log stream: job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12. That pod began logging level=ERROR "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" at 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z, matching the ~13:45 UTC report, and the last observed instance is 2026-11-23T14:44:00Z. The lines report connection-acquisition waits (wait_time_ms) of 1227–4840 ms and queue_length of 5–15, so requests queued for a database connection for up to about 4.8 seconds. A rolling-count query over the preceding days returned the "pool exhausted" message only from the ~13:49 bin on 2026-11-23, so this error onset appears new rather than steady background within the sampled range. Some payments still succeeded during and after the burst (INFO "Payment processed successfully" at 13:42, 13:59, 14:49 and 15:27), so the impact was intermittent rather than a total outage. What actually exhausted the pool — database-side saturation, pool-size configuration, or another dependency — is not observable here: Loki holds no database or other service logs, and pod status, events, ConfigMaps, metrics and traces could not be read, and change history is not integrated. The database-connection pool exhaustion inside payment-api pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 is the supported finding; the object that caused it is unidentified, so no root cause object is named.

claims.text: In namespace app-259 the only log stream observed is job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12; count_over_time grouped by job/pod_name/service for 2026-11-23T12:00–16:20 and a 24h-grouped query returning data from 2026-11-22T16:23 to 2026-11-23T16:18 both returned exactly this single series.

pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 logged level=ERROR, message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" at 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z with wait_time_ms=1227 and queue_length=10; this is the earliest such line returned by the queries.

The same "pool exhausted" ERROR was logged repeatedly between 13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z (observed lines at 13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31 and 14:44); the last observed instance is 14:44:00Z with wait_time_ms=3836 and queue_length=5.

The pool-exhaustion lines report database connection acquisition waits (wait_time_ms) from 1227 ms to 4840 ms and queue_length values from 5 to 15; max wait_time_ms 4840 and max queue_length 15 were extracted from these lines for pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12.

A rolling 5m count_over_time of the "pool exhausted" message for 2026-11-23T12:00–16:20 returned non-zero bins only between 2026-11-23T13:46:49Z and 14:48:50Z (values 1–2), with no non-zero bin returned after that point.

In a query using a 6h rolling window whose returned data spans 2026-11-23T13:49:40 to 15:46:16 (the tool evaluated from its 6h lookback limit), the "pool exhausted" message had values only from the 13:49:40 bin onward (1, 6, 8, 8) and no non-zero value at any earlier evaluation point in that series, so within that sampled view the message first appears on 2026-11-23 shortly after 13:46.

Only two distinct application log messages were observed for this pod in the queried data: "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" and "Payment processed successfully"; no startup, config-reload, shutdown, timeout, refused-connection or memory/CPU related lines were returned.

Payments still succeeded around the error burst: INFO "Payment processed successfully" at 13:42:00Z and 13:59:00Z before/during the burst, and at 14:49:00Z and 15:27:00Z after the last observed 14:44:00Z error.

Loki returned logs for namespace app-259 only: a per-namespace count_over_time over {namespace=~".+"} for 2026-11-23T13:00–14:30 returned one series, namespace="app-259", so no database, dependency or other workload logs were available to check.

A keyword search across all available namespaces for postgres|mysql|database|db-|rds|connection refused over 2026-11-22T16:20–2026-11-23T16:20 returned only the 8 payment-api "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" lines; no database-side or connection-refused lines were returned.

The payment-api process at pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 exhausted its own database connection pool around 13:46–14:45, so requests waited up to about 4.8 s for a connection (queue up to 15) and connection acquisition failed; the upstream condition that kept the pool saturated (database slowness, pool-size configuration, or a dependency fault) is not visible in the available evidence.

A configuration change (for example a reduced maximum pool size or a changed database endpoint) or a restart of the workload around 13:45 is a candidate cause that this Run could neither confirm nor exclude, because no ConfigMap, deployment revision, image digest, restart count or Kubernetes event could be read and the change-history integration is not available.

Because payment successes are interleaved with the errors, the pool exhaustion was intermittent rather than a total outage of the pod; the number of failed versus attempted payments is unknown because only sampled log lines are visible and no error-rate metric or trace could be read.

The log stream carries the same pod_name (payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12) and the same job/service before, during and after the errors, and no startup or shutdown messages were returned; nothing in the logs directly indicates a pod replacement, although restart counts could not be read.

gaps: Kubernetes API was unavailable: kubernetes_jq_query and kubernetes_tabular_query for pods in app-259 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and fetch_pod_logs for pod payment-api returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the pod's phase, restart count, last termination reason and exit code, events, owner Deployment/ReplicaSet and ConfigMaps are unknown.

Prometheus was unavailable: execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so payment-api error-rate and latency series and kube-state-metrics object state could not be checked.
Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services and traces_search for service payment returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so span-level errors, latency and any payment-to-database client spans are unknown.

The database dependency is unidentified: Loki held only the app-259 payment-api stream (no database or other service logs), so the object or service behind the connection pool could not be investigated.
Whether other payment-api replicas existed and whether they also failed is unknown; only one pod_name label value (payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12) was ever returned by Loki queries.
change_history is not integrated, so whether a deployment, ConfigMap or pool-size change occurred at ~13:45 cannot be determined.

Log coverage is sparse (on the order of one line every few minutes), so the exact first failing request and the exact recovery time are bounded only by sampled lines (13:46:00Z first error, 14:44:00Z last error, 14:49:00Z next observed success).

Queries returned nothing and are therefore unknown rather than zero: a line filter for the literal text "error" over 2026-11-23T13:30–14:15 returned no lines (the message text says "Failed ... pool exhausted" while the level label is ERROR); a pod-name regex {namespace="app-259", pod=~"payment.*"} returned no streams (the pod is labelled pod_name, not pod); and keyword searches for warn and for max|reload|config|timeout|refused|dial|listen|starting|shutdown|gc|memory|cpu returned no lines.

A 24h count of "pool exhausted" and the 6h-window series could not establish a full historical baseline: the 24h query returned a single evaluation point and the 6h query only evaluated from 13:49:40, so long-term pre-incident error frequency is unknown.
next_steps: Read pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 status, container restart counts, last termination reason and events in namespace app-259, plus its ReplicaSet/Deployment owner and any ConfigMap holding connection-pool or database settings.
Check whether the database dependency used by app-259's payment-api was saturated, slow or restarted around 2026-11-23T13:40–15:00.
Inspect payment-api error-rate and latency metrics and its spans (payment server spans and any database client spans) for 2026-11-23T13:40–15:00 to quantify failures and the slow dependency.
Obtain change history for app-259 through a connected integration to see whether pool-size or database connection settings changed near 13:45.
